clue.text: Unrefined Ecstasy taken by quiet homosexual the Sun outed

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: the drug is taken in by the word that follows, so it sits inside it
outed here means put out, so the named letter is expelled from the word

parts.note: a lesbian is a homosexual woman
S is the standard abbreviation for sun
E is slang for the drug Ecstasy

explanation.surface: A tabloid headline: a drug-taking gay man exposed by the Sun newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outed' removes S from LESBIAN, leaving LEBIAN; 'taken by' puts E inside that to give LEBEIAN, after P. The Sun is a British tabloid, which gives the surface its scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Plebeian describes common, coarse manners, the synonym of unrefined as in lacking polish or breeding.

clue.text: East German in China gets this sort of vote?

indicators.note: in places the German word inside the mate

parts.note: china is Cockney rhyming slang for mate (china plate), i.e. pal
Ost is German for east

explanation.surface: Seems to ask how a German in China casts a ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is not the country but rhyming slang (china plate = mate).
explanation.definitionFit: A postal vote is one cast by mail rather than in person at a polling station.

clue.text: Former hippy commune's ideal: sleeping around endlessly

indicators.note: around signals the letters are moved about into a new order
endlessly means the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: The free-love ideal of a hippy commune: sleeping around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the last letter of the second word and 'around' mixes the twelve letters. The island, in the Thames at Twickenham, hosted a hippy commune around 1970.
explanation.definitionFit: This Thames island in London housed a well-known hippy commune at its hotel in the late 1960s.

clue.text: Historian who wrote of a meeting of king and primate

parts.note: Edward is the name of several English kings
a gibbon is a small ape, a primate

explanation.surface: A chronicler records a summit between a monarch and an archbishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primate' suggests an archbishop meeting the king, but here it means an ape.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Gibbon wrote The Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire, the classic eighteenth-century history.

clue.text: One to be found in cabin shortly?

definitions.text: One to be found in cabin shortly?

parts.words: One to be found in cabin shortly?
parts.note: the sailor's short form AB appears within the word cabin, and a sailor lives in a ship's cabin

explanation.surface: Seems to ask who will soon be found in a ship's cabin.
explanation.walkthrough: Shortly a rating is AB, which sits inside cABin.
explanation.definitionFit: A trained ordinary rating in a merchant or naval crew is abbreviated AB.

clue.text: Having no children to manage, good as mattress may be

parts.note: s.p. is sine prole, the Latin genealogical abbreviation for without issue
to run a business is to manage it

explanation.surface: A childless couple can afford a good mattress, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: SP (sine prole, 'without offspring') is a family-tree convention worth learning.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprung mattress has coil springs inside it, one of the standard kinds sold.

clue.text: Things made for Tube stations, primarily

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a duct is a tube or channel

indicators.note: primarily asks for the initial of the word it follows

explanation.surface: Goods manufactured for London Underground stations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tube' looks like the London Underground but is just a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Products are goods that are manufactured or produced.

clue.text: Sure sign of love given by one foreign Romeo

parts.note: une is French for one
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a ring, as an engagement or wedding ring, is a token of love

explanation.surface: A foreign lover gives a ring as a sure sign of devotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romeo' is the lover in the surface but the radio-alphabet R in the parse.
explanation.definitionFit: Unerring means never missing or making a mistake, so sure or certain.

clue.text: Clergy corrupted with essentially diabolical sweetener

indicators.note: corrupted letters are spoilt and jumbled into a new order
essentially picks out the central letters, the essence, of the word

explanation.surface: Corrupt clergy and something diabolically sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' takes OL, the middle two letters of DIABOLICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Glycerine is a sweet-tasting syrupy compound used as a food sweetener.

clue.text: Obstinacy of writer putting last name first

indicators.note: the surname of the writer is shifted to stand before his first name, as on a register

parts.note: Will Self is a British novelist and journalist

explanation.surface: A writer being stubborn about how his name is listed.
explanation.walkthrough: Will Self is an English novelist; swapping surname and forename gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-will is stubborn insistence on one's own way, which is obstinacy.

clue.text: See 22
A Cockney bum overwhelmed by depression? He's probably got hives

indicators.note: the bum is swallowed up inside the depression

parts.note: a pit is a hollow or depression in the ground
aris is Cockney rhyming slang for backside (Aristotle, bottle and glass, arse)

explanation.surface: A Londoner's sore backside sunk in a hollow, and a rash of hives to boot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overwhelmed by' splits the hollow around the slang word. 'Hives' looks medical (an itchy rash) but means beehives.
explanation.definitionFit: A beekeeper keeps colonies in hives, so one probably owns several of those boxes.

clue.text: See 24
Seen in the Guardian, an Irish boy's diet?

indicators.note: seen in means the name appears inside the guardian

parts.note: a parent is a guardian of a child
Liam is a common Irish boy's name

explanation.surface: Seems to ask what an Irish lad eats, as reported by the Guardian newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diet' poses as food but is a legislative assembly, as in the Japanese Diet; the Guardian is a British newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A diet is a national legislative assembly, the same thing as a legislature.

clue.text: Grandma's turning 100, seen by satellite in Texan city

indicators.note: turning here means the letters are read the other way round

parts.note: nana is a grandmother, and the 's gives NANAS
a ton is a hundred
Io is one of Jupiter's moons

explanation.surface: An old lady's hundredth birthday, watched from orbit somewhere in Texas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses NANAS to SANAN.
explanation.definitionFit: San Antonio is a major city in south-central Texas, home of the Alamo.

clue.text: Growth of tumour now starts to restrict joint

indicators.note: the two initials hem in the joint on either side
starts asks for the opening letters of the two words

parts.note: a reefer is a cannabis cigarette, a joint

explanation.surface: A medical note about a tumour that has begun to press on a knee or hip joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growth' looks like the tumour but means a plant; 'joint' is a cannabis cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant is a growth, and this is a tall fern with a trunk like a tree's.

clue.text: Hard-to-let sort of ground

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: A plot of land that is difficult to rent out.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallowed ground is holy land, such as a consecrated churchyard.

clue.text: When The Times will appear as indicated by some chambermaids

definitions.text: When The Times will appear as indicated by some chambermaids

parts.words: When The Times will appear as indicated by some chambermaids
parts.note: the newspaper is delivered early in the day, and a chambermaid's greeting or room sign marks that part of the day

explanation.surface: A hotel guest wondering when the newspaper will arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: Some of 'chambermaids' is AM, the abbreviation that marks times before noon; The Times newspaper is out early in the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Daily newspapers like The Times are delivered at the start of each day, before noon.

clue.text: Subversive gets beheaded? That's OK

indicators.note: beheaded means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: treasonable acts undermine the state, i.e. are subversive

explanation.surface: A rebel loses his head, and someone shrugs that this is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' drops the T, aptly the punishment for treason.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fair or acceptable can be called reasonable or simply OK.

clue.text: See 2
See 3
Protection for pupils in Sunderland?

parts.note: pupils are parts of the eye, and the land under the sun is where eyes need guarding from glare

explanation.surface: Seems to ask about safety for schoolchildren in the north-east English city of Sunderland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pupils' are eyes, not schoolchildren; Sunderland splits as S + underland, and Hades is the land under the earth, giving S-HADES.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunglasses, in slang, guard the eyes from bright glare.

clue.text: Passport to Pimlico possibly a Cockney's way of better getting to Notting Hill?

indicators.note: Cockneys drop their aitches, so the opening H goes

parts.note: healing is how one gets better after illness
Notting Hill is a 1999 romantic comedy film

explanation.surface: Seems to ask whether a Londoner's travel document gets him to a West London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Passport to Pimlico (1949) came from Ealing Studios in London, famous for its comedies; Pimlico and Notting Hill are London districts, which the surface leans on.
explanation.definitionFit: Passport to Pimlico is a classic example of the British studio's film comedies, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: Former PM hasn't one? I'm surprised

indicators.note: surprised letters are taken aback and thrown into disorder

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral, and I'm is kept as written, giving three letters for the pool

explanation.surface: A sceptic's quip that some ex-premier has none of something, and is surprised.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian Smith was Prime Minister of Rhodesia (now Zimbabwe), 1964-79.
explanation.definitionFit: Ian Smith led Rhodesia's white-minority government as its premier before the country became Zimbabwe.

clue.text: Journalist to succeed with article prior to hearing of Indian politician

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the crossword journalist
to win is to succeed
a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: hearing of means the word as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: an Indian, as a meal, is a curry

explanation.surface: A reporter hopes to beat a rival to a story about an Indian politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Edwina Currie is a former British Conservative minister; 'an Indian' is British slang for a curry dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: She was an MP and junior health minister in the 1980s, so a politician.

clue.text: Two bachelors outside a university, plastered

indicators.note: the two degrees are placed on either side of the following letters
two calls for the bachelor degree to be used twice

parts.note: BEd is the Bachelor of Education degree

explanation.surface: Two young graduates drunk outside their college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps BED...BED around A and U. 'plastered' poses as drunk but means smeared over.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedaub is to smear or daub all over, so something bedaubed is covered or plastered.

clue.text: Female's in the buff, if this?

definitions.text: Female's in the buff, if this?

indicators.note: in places the woman's name inside the enthusiast

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast or fan, also called a nut
Di is a female name, and the 's gives DIS

explanation.surface: A question about why a woman is naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the buff' reads as naked, but buff is an enthusiast (a nut), and DI'S goes in it. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturists favour going without clothing, so a woman who is one would be naked.

clue.text: Those taking course south, following Stewart and Arthur hitch-hiking

indicators.note: following puts the compass letter after the two names

parts.note: Stu is short for Stewart
Arthur Dent is the hero of The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy

explanation.surface: Someone heads south behind two hitch-hiking travellers.
explanation.walkthrough: Course means a programme of study, not a route, despite the travel imagery.
explanation.definitionFit: Those enrolled on an academic course are pupils or undergraduates of it.
